analysis.title: Workday F3Q Preview - Expecting Continued Momentum
key_insights: DB expects Workday to report F3Q results after the close on November 24, ahead of consensus on both revenue and earnings, driven by continued execution and modest upside to 12-month subscription backlog, possibly toward the higher end of guidance.
Because Workday shared a preliminary FY28 outlook at F2Q results, DB does not expect anything in F3Q to meaningfully change the equity narrative.
Partner field checks were broadly consistent with recent quarters: momentum down-market from Workday GO, continued public sector success, and functional leaders showing interest in AI solutions.

Partners reported lengthening sales cycles as customers' purchasing organizations scrutinize AI pricing and terms, though more customers are engaging earlier. DB's read is that the AI opportunity is still early outside Workday's acquisitions, which continue to see good traction.

One check noted that on some contracts Workday is moving to a flat-rate price increase methodology instead of CPI plus Innovation Index. Partners also noted a modest increase in early renewal activity.
Feedback on Workday's sales organization was generally constructive. One partner cited positivity heading into 4Q and the return of some sellers who had previously left.
For 4Q, DB sees possible modest upside to subscription revenue and non-GAAP operating margin estimates, but says Street estimates for 12-month subscription backlog could prove somewhat optimistic.
DB does not expect meaningful changes to the preliminary FY28 outlook.
Workday announced its intent to acquire Honeydew, a semantic layer for AI and business intelligence. DB calls it a small tuck-in deal expected to close in 4Q.
Workday GO for Financials was released, along with EU Sovereign Cloud enhancements announced at Rising EMEA. DB thinks these could help down-market and international traction respectively.

market_movers.rationale: DB keeps its Hold rating and $220 price target ahead of F3Q results, which it expects to beat consensus. The stock closed at $177.45 on Nov 18.

earnings_insights: Workday reports F3Q after the close on November 24, 2026. DB expects results above consensus on both revenue and earnings (estimate, not yet reported).
DB expects modest upside to 12-month subscription backlog, possibly toward the higher end of company guidance (DB estimate, not yet reported).
For 4Q, DB sees possible modest upside to subscription revenue and non-GAAP operating margin estimates versus Street (forecast).
DB says Street estimates for 12-month subscription backlog could prove somewhat optimistic (forecast).

Sales cycles are lengthening as customers scrutinize AI pricing and terms.

key_data_points.context: Hold rating. The target was raised from $190/$180 in Feb 2026 to $220 on 17 Aug 2026 and is unchanged here.

tension_points.bull_case: DB expects modest upside to 12-month subscription backlog, possibly toward the higher end of guidance, and results ahead of consensus on revenue and earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Street estimates for 12-month subscription backlog could prove somewhat optimistic, and sales cycles are lengthening as customers scrutinize AI pricing and terms.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 12-month subscription backlog reported below Street estimates at the F3Q print on November 24.

theme_stances.evidence: we expect results ahead of consensus on both the top and bottom line
